platform: Linux x86-64; little-endian u64 words and 64-bit borrowed-buffer lengths
scope: Complete Template::parse, parse_placeholder and push_literal computation. Rendering, allocation and Rust object materialization remain host responsibilities.

calling_convention.return: Zero-extended u32 transport status in the native ABI return register
calling_convention.caller_obligations: All indicated buffers are live, correctly sized and mutually non-overlapping during the synchronous call. No pointers are retained.
calling_convention.source: Arbitrary bytes, validated completely as UTF-8 before parsing. No trusted-UTF8 profile or source-size cap.
calling_convention.output: Writable capacity of at least 64 bytes; query/emit write only the reported prefix. The unused output suffix is unchanged.

header_words.name: record_count
header_words.meaning: Number of 24-byte instructions, including append instructions; not the final segment count.

header_words.name: required
header_words.meaning: Checked 64 + 24 * record_count; semantic errors always require 64.

header_words.name: written
header_words.meaning: 64 for query or semantic error; required for successful emit.

header_words.name: semantic_error
header_words.meaning: Zero for a valid template, otherwise one of the four original parse errors.

header_words.name: error_start
header_words.meaning: Original UTF-8 byte offset; zero when semantic_error is zero.

record_invariants: All ranges are nonempty, within source_len, on UTF-8 boundaries and ordered without overlap.
Kind 1 creates Literal(source[start..end]); there is no immediately preceding Literal segment.
Kind 2 appends source[start..end] to the immediately preceding Literal segment; that segment must exist.
Kind 3 creates a new Placeholder from the native-selected trimmed range. Repeated names retain separate ordered Placeholder segments.
Escaped four-brace delimiters reference their first two source bytes and skip the other two. Gaps between ranges are valid.

The host passes each checked kind-3 original source range to the HIA template_index Builder. HIA performs duplicate detection and byte ordering; Rust moves owned names into a canonical Vec by native node ID and constructs every original Vec<Segment> occurrence without reparsing or Rust sorting.
Empty source produces zero records. Empty literal fragments are omitted; adjacent literal fragments are joined by append instructions.

operations.query: Validate frame and entire UTF-8 source; compute the complete plan or semantic error without emitting records; write only the 64-byte header.
operations.emit: Validate frame, entire UTF-8 source, complete semantic result and required output capacity before any write. Emit records only for a valid template, then publish the header.
operations.agreement: For the same source, query and emit agree on source_len, record_count, required, semantic_error and error_start. Only operation and written differ.

semantic_errors.1: EmptyPlaceholder: the interior of the first closing pair becomes empty after Rust-compatible Unicode whitespace trim; start is the outer opening pair.
semantic_errors.2: NestedPlaceholder: an inner opening pair is encountered before closing; start is the outer opening pair.
semantic_errors.3: UnmatchedClosingDelimiter: a top-level closing pair is not consumed as a four-brace literal escape; start is that pair.
semantic_errors.4: UnterminatedPlaceholder: an opened placeholder reaches the end without closing or an earlier nested opening; start is the outer opening pair.
semantic_errors.partial_prefix: No partial plan or partial Template is returned, including when an error follows valid literal/placeholder prefixes.

outer_priority: four opening braces -> literal opening pair
four closing braces -> literal closing pair
syntax.inner_escape: Four-brace literal escaping applies only outside placeholders.
syntax.names: Trim only leading/trailing Unicode White_Space; keep internal whitespace, single braces, Unicode and NUL. No identifier alphabet, case folding or normalization.
syntax.error_priority: Preserve the first error reached by the original left-to-right parser; inner error positions refer to the outer opener.

transport_statuses.0: Valid native request completed; inspect semantic_error for the Rust parse result.
transport_statuses.4294967294: SHORT: output capacity below 64, workspace length below 32, or successful emit capacity below required.
transport_statuses.4294967295: INVALID: workspace longer than 32, wrong version/op/reserved word, invalid UTF-8, or unrepresentable checked output size.
transport_statuses.precedence: Minimum output/workspace capacity checks occur first; exact frame validation precedes full UTF-8 validation; semantic planning precedes final emit capacity validation.
transport_statuses.no_write: Every nonzero transport return leaves source, workspace and the entire output byte-for-byte unchanged. Semantic errors are successful transport and write their header.

host_adapter.responsibilities: Allocate query/emit buffers, check complete header and checked sizes, require query/emit agreement, validate returned range framing and UTF-8 boundaries, map the four native error codes, and materialize original Rust strings/segments plus HIA-index-ordered owned placeholder names.
host_adapter.forbidden_fallback: No Rust delimiter parser, trim implementation or semantic fallback is selected when HIA fails.
host_adapter.native_failure: Internal ABI/transport rejection is distinct from the four original semantic parse errors.
host_adapter.retained_boundary: Original error Display/Debug/Error implementations, public data traits, render algorithm and all 14 original tests remain unchanged.
